_comment: What the frequency reader may and may not count for an inflected headword.
Every row is a class of error the reader has actually made (I-126, and the
v1.0.5 pass that closed it): the ㄹ-drop forms it never reached, the
irregular alternants it treated as finished forms, the whole tokens that
are somebody else's word, and the strings two headwords genuinely share.
to it against the shipped headword list and the Wiktionary lemma list;
`counts` rows are checked against the real corpus when it is present.

cases.why: ㄹ-drop adnominal: how a long thing is described, and 길 is also a noun (road)
ㄹ-drop adnominal with no competing noun
the commonest ㄹ-stem adjective; its ㄹ-drop forms carry most of its use
ㅅ-irregular: the alternant 이 + ㅆ is not 있 — 있어요 belongs to 있다, and ranked 잇다 first in Korean
its ㄹ-drop alternant 거 is 것 contracted: 겁니다 and 거니까 are 'it is the thing'
its stem is the pronoun 우리: 우린 and 우리는 are 'we'
its ㄹ-drop alternant 나 is the pronoun: 나는 is 'I'
the ㄴ-adnominal 한 is 'one'; the 아/어 form 해 is the Sun
간 is 'liver' and a lemma; 갈 is 갈다's stem; 가요 is the taught noun (a song) and is nobody's verb form
ㅅ-irregular alternant 그 must not fold 그게 (that thing) onto this verb — it ranked 4th
a two-syllable adnominal that is nobody else's is counted
ㄷ-irregular: 걸 before a vowel is shared with 걸다 and divided, 걷 before a consonant is its own
사 before 세요 is shared with 사다 and divided; 산 is a mountain
a regular ㄷ stem keeps its ㄷ before a vowel: the spelling cannot say which class a ㄷ-final stem is in, so both readings count
a regular ㅂ stem: 입어요 is the word, 이워요 is not
a regular ㅅ stem: 웃어요 is the word, 우어요 is not
